messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: John Miller <john.miller@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC networking follow-up: next steps & info needed

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned on the Private VPC option (vs Hosted/Dedicated):

What we heard from you:
- Priority: data residency + full control over network egress (we should run in your VPC)
- Expected qps: ~350 rps peak for inference, mostly short prompts; bursty during business hours
- SLOs: 95th perc latency target of ~200ms for simple completions
- Timeline: procurement and security review in Oct; hopeful pilot in Nov

Open questions / items we need from your infra team to validate feasibility:
1) Preferred connectivity: AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering? We support both; PrivateLink is usually simpler for segmented networks.
2) Egress IP allowlist — do you have a static NAT or do you prefer us to present fixed egress ranges?
3) VPN vs Direct Connect for private control plane access? If you need on-prem access, please indicate bandwidth and latency targets.

I'll loop in Sean (networking lead) and Dev (engr) to answer the technical questions. Could your network/security lead share: a VPC CIDR, the preferred connection pattern, and any existing IP allowlists we should expect?

Attachments: I attached a short checklist that shows the fields we typically ask for (redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx) and a sample diagram request.

Next steps (suggested):
- Anna to share infra contact + the three items above (VPC CIDR, PrivateLink vs peering decision, egress approach) — by EOD next Tue (10/5)
- Redwood to provide an initial network diagram and sample CloudFormation / Terraform snippet for the PrivateLink endpoint
- Schedule a 30-minute technical sync between your network lead and Sean/Dev — propose Wed 10/7 10am PT

Thanks — happy to adjust if your timeline is different.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

I'll ask John to share the VPC CIDR and the security contact. We should be able to get you the CIDR and NAT egress by Tue 10/5.

Hi all —

Thanks Anna. Sharing the initial infra details below; happy to expand in the sync.

- VPC CIDR: 10.40.0.0/16
- NAT egress IPs: 52.24.11.98, 52.24.11.99
- Preferred connectivity: PrivateLink first; we may evaluate peering if latency becomes an issue.
- Control plane: VPN (IPSec) for initial setup, target DC later.
- Bandwidth: 1Gbps sustained should be fine for the pilot; latency to Redwood region (us-west-2) ~25–40ms typical.

One note on allowlisting: our security team prefers we avoid wide open CIDR ranges and use specific IPs for vendor egress. If Redwood can provide a documented list of egress IPs and/or a small range for inference egress that would be ideal.

I'm available Wed 10/7 10am PT for a technical sync — please send an invite.

Thanks John — this is perfect. A couple quick clarifications from our side before the sync: 

1) Egress IPs: we can offer a small set of static egress IPs for inference traffic. For the pilot we can provide two fixed IPs and a /29 if you prefer a short CIDR. Which would you prefer for your allowlist?

2) PrivateLink flow: Redwood will host a Network Load Balancer in our managed account and publish a PrivateLink endpoint service. Your team will create a VPC endpoint in 10.40.0.0/16 and associate it with your subnets. We will provide Terraform snippets and a CloudFormation example in the doc I’ll attach.

3) TLS + mTLS: we support mutual TLS for the control plane; data plane uses TLS. If your security team requires mTLS for data plane calls, we can discuss cert distribution options.

4) Ops handoff: post-pilot we suggest a runbook handoff that includes token rotation, KMS key references (if using our managed KMS), and observability endpoints we will expose to your SRE team.

I attached a short PrivateLink checklist and a sample terraform snippet for the endpoint. I’ll propose the 10/7 10am PT invite to everyone now.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.
—Sean
